answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce resource before it can earn fees or influence shared decisions; the protocol locks that bond and slashes it when fraud is proven through reproducible evidence and an appeal window. Creating a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand independently funded bonds, rather than merely changing names, and coordinated abuse risks losing them all. A walnut, onyx, or shale token could serve as the bond only if it has real opportunity cost and cannot be minted freely by the attacker.
